saints.name: Our Lady of Fatima
saints.title: Marian Memorial
saints.shortBlurb: The 1917 apparitions of the Virgin Mary to three shepherd children at Fatima, calling the world to prayer and penance…
biography: On 13 May 1917, while the First World War raged, three shepherd children — Lúcia dos Santos, ten, and her cousins Francisco and Jacinta Marto, nine and seven — were watching their flocks at the Cova da Iria near Fatima in Portugal when a Lady brighter than the sun appeared above a holm oak.

She came again on the thirteenth of each month until October, asking for the daily Rosary, prayer, and penance for the conversion of sinners and the peace of the world, and in July confiding three secrets, among them a vision of hell and the consecration of Russia to her Immaculate Heart.

On 13 October, before some seventy thousand onlookers, the sun seemed to dance and plunge toward the earth — the Miracle of the Sun, reported by the secular press. Francisco and Jacinta died of influenza, in 1919 and 1920, and were canonized at Fatima by Pope Francis in 2017; Lúcia, a Carmelite nun, died in 2005.

The Bishop of Leiria declared the apparitions worthy of belief in 1930. On 13 May 1981, the feast itself, John Paul II was shot; he credited her hand with turning the bullet, which now lies in the crown of her image.
saints.knownFor: The call to prayer, penance, and the Rosary given at Fatima in 1917.

sources.text: Vatican biography, Canonization of the Shepherds of Fatima (vatican.va)
